149	// RunAggregatePartitionedSliding combines sliding windows (see
150	// RunAggregateSliding) with partitioned inputs: events from different
151	// partitions merge into one count and sum per key and window, and both the
152	// late-event check and window closure use the effective (minimum) watermark.
153	// windowMillis and slideMillis are validated exactly as in
154	// RunAggregateSliding. partitions selects the input mode:
155	//
156	//   - partitions == 0: legacy single-watermark mode. Records do not carry a
157	//     partition field; any extra fields are ignored.
158	//
159	//   - partitions > 0: partitioned mode, merging partitions independent input
160	//     sources of the same stream. Every event and watermark record must carry
161	//     an integer "partition" in [0,partitions). Each partition advances its
162	//     own watermark; no effective watermark exists until every partition has
163	//     reported at least once, afterwards the effective watermark is the
164	//     minimum of the per-partition values. Window closure and late-event
165	//     checks use this minimum, so one partition's larger watermark can never
166	//     close a window or drop an event ahead of the others. A partition
167	//     watermark may repeat or jump forward but never move backwards.
168	//
169	//     A partition may be declared idle with
170	//     {"type":"idle","partition":p}. An idle partition stops contributing to
171	//     the effective watermark: non-idle partitions that have not reported a
172	//     watermark yet still keep the effective watermark unknown, while a
173	//     partition that never reported may itself be declared idle. When every
174	//     remaining (non-idle) partition has reported, the effective watermark is
175	//     their minimum and the idle record itself can close windows. If all
176	//     partitions are idle, the last produced effective watermark is retained;
177	//     when none was ever produced it stays unknown. Idleness is declared by
178	//     the input only, never inferred from time; a repeated idle declaration
179	//     is a no-op. The next watermark record for that partition resumes it:
180	//     its time must be at least both the partition's previous watermark and
181	//     the current effective watermark. An event for an idle partition is
182	//     fatal; it never resumes implicitly.
183	//
184	// partitions < 0 is an error. Windows, ordering, late-event reporting,
185	// overflow checks and end-of-input behavior are otherwise identical to
186	// RunAggregateSliding.
187	func RunAggregatePartitionedSliding(r io.Reader, windowMillis, slideMillis, partitions int64, out io.Writer, lateLog io.Writer) error {
188		if windowMillis <= 0 {
189			return fmt.Errorf("window length must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", windowMillis)
190		}
191		if slideMillis <= 0 {
192			return fmt.Errorf("slide interval must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", slideMillis)
193		}
194		if slideMillis > windowMillis {
195			return fmt.Errorf("slide interval %d must not exceed window length %d", slideMillis, windowMillis)
196		}
197		if partitions < 0 {
198			return fmt.Errorf("partition count must be a positive signed 64-bit integer, got %d", partitions)
199		}
200		s := &aggregateState{
201			windowMillis:  windowMillis,
202			slideMillis:   slideMillis,
203			windows:       make(map[windowID]*windowState),
204			out:           out,
205			lateLog:       lateLog,
206			partitions:    partitions,
207			partWatermark: make(map[int64]*int64),
208			idle:          make(map[int64]bool),
209		}
210	
211		// Read records with a line collector that keeps a read failure distinct
212		// from end of input: only newline-terminated lines (plus, at a clean EOF,
213		// one unterminated final line) ever become records.
214		lineNo := 0
215		err := readAggregateLines(r, func(line string, no int) error {
216			lineNo = no
217			if strings.TrimSpace(line) == "" {
218				return nil
219			}
220			return s.processLine(line, lineNo)
221		})
222		return err
223	}

225	// maxAggregateLineBytes caps the size of a single physical input line, matching
226	// the scanner buffer limit this used to run with. A line this long is fatal
227	// before its record is parsed.
228	const maxAggregateLineBytes = 1024 * 1024 * 1024
229	
230	// errAggregateLineTooLong reports a physical input line that never ends within
231	// maxAggregateLineBytes.
232	var errAggregateLineTooLong = errors.New("aggregate input line longer than 1 GiB")
233	
234	// errAggregateBadReadCount reports an io.Reader that handed back a byte count
235	// outside the destination buffer, violating the io.Reader contract.
236	var errAggregateBadReadCount = errors.New("aggregate reader returned an impossible byte count")
237	
238	// readAggregateLines feeds newline-delimited physical lines from r to handle,
239	// counting every line (a bare "\n" is a blank line too) and stripping a single
240	// trailing '\r' so CRLF input works as before. Clean end of input and a
241	// non-EOF read failure are handled differently: at clean io.EOF a final line
242	// missing its newline is still delivered, exactly like every other final
243	// record; after a non-EOF read error only lines whose newline was already
244	// received (including those delivered by the same Read that carried the
245	// error) are handled, in order, and then the reader's original error is
246	// returned. The unterminated tail never reaches handle, so a read failure
247	// mid-record can neither be misreported as an input error nor produce
248	// events, watermarks, idle declarations, late notices or window results. A
249	// non-nil error from handle stops reading immediately and replaces the read
250	// error, so an earlier record or output failure is not overwritten by a
251	// failure the reader only reports later.
252	func readAggregateLines(r io.Reader, handle func(line string, lineNo int) error) error {
253		// buf[start:end] is the undelivered tail; buf[:start] is space freed by
254		// already delivered lines. The buffer is compacted and grown like
255		// bufio.Scanner's, so a long unterminated line is bounded by
256		// maxAggregateLineBytes instead of growing without limit.
257		buf := make([]byte, 64*1024)
258		start, end := 0, 0
259		lineNo := 0
260		emptyReads := 0
261		deliver := func(b []byte) error {
262			lineNo++
263			line := strings.TrimSuffix(string(b), "\r")
264			return handle(line, lineNo)
265		}
266		for {
267			// Move the pending tail to the front when its freed prefix is large
268			// enough or when the whole buffer is pending.
269			if start > 0 && (end == len(buf) || start > len(buf)/2) {
270				copy(buf, buf[start:end])
271				end -= start
272				start = 0
273			}
274			if end == len(buf) {
275				// No newline fit before the end: the physical line is too long.
276				if len(buf) >= maxAggregateLineBytes {
277					return errAggregateLineTooLong
278				}
279				newLen := len(buf) * 2
280				if newLen > maxAggregateLineBytes || newLen < len(buf) {
281					newLen = maxAggregateLineBytes
282				}
283				grown := make([]byte, newLen)
284				copy(grown, buf[start:end])
285				buf = grown
286				end -= start
287				start = 0
288			}
289			n, readErr := r.Read(buf[end:])
290			if n < 0 || n > len(buf)-end {
291				// A Reader must never report a byte count outside the buffer.
292				return errAggregateBadReadCount
293			}
294			end += n
295			for {
296				i := bytes.IndexByte(buf[start:end], '\n')
297				if i < 0 {
298					break
299				}
300				if err := deliver(buf[start : start+i]); err != nil {
301					return err
302				}
303				start += i + 1
304			}
305			if readErr != nil {
306				if errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
307					// Clean end of input: a trailing line without a newline is a
308					// complete final record; an empty tail (input ending exactly
309					// on '\n') is nothing, not an extra blank line.
310					if end > start {
311						if err := deliver(buf[start:end]); err != nil {
312							return err
313						}
314					}
315					return nil
316				}
317				// Any other failure means the stream stopped mid-record: the
318				// still-unterminated bytes are not a record. Surface the original
319				// error unchanged so errors.Is keeps working for callers.
320				return readErr
321			}
322			if n == 0 {
323				// No data and no error: refuse to spin forever on a broken Reader.
324				emptyReads++
325				if emptyReads > 100 {
326					return io.ErrNoProgress
327				}
328			} else {
329				emptyReads = 0
330			}
331		}
332	}

347	func (s *aggregateState) processLine(line string, lineNo int) error {
348		var obj map[string]json.RawMessage
349		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
350			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: "invalid JSON record: " + err.Error()}
351		}

353		typeRaw, ok := obj["type"]
354		if !ok {
355			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `missing required string field "type"`}
356		}
357		recordType, err := decodeString(typeRaw, "type")
358		if err != nil {
359			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: err.Error()}
360		}

362		switch recordType {
363		case "event":
364			return s.processEvent(obj, lineNo)
365		case "watermark":
366			return s.processWatermark(obj, lineNo)
367		case "idle":

371				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("unknown record type %q", recordType)}

379	// floorDiv returns math.Floor(a/b) for b > 0; Go's / truncates toward zero,
380	// so negative numerators need explicit adjustment.
381	func floorDiv(a, b int64) int64 {
382		q := a / b
383		if a%b != 0 && a < 0 {
384			q--
385		}
386		return q
387	}

389	// containingWindowBounds returns the first and last (inclusive) window index
390	// whose window [k*slideMillis, k*slideMillis+windowMillis) contains
391	// eventTime. Windows start at 0, slideMillis, 2*slideMillis, ... and none
392	// with a negative start is created, so the first index is clamped to zero.
393	// The last index is eventTime/slideMillis, so an event at a window end is
394	// outside that window.
395	func (s *aggregateState) containingWindowBounds(eventTime int64) (first, last int64) {
396		last = eventTime / s.slideMillis
397		first = floorDiv(eventTime-s.windowMillis, s.slideMillis) + 1
398		if first < 0 {
399			first = 0
400		}
401		return first, last
402	}
403	
404	// containingWindowCount returns how many windows contain eventTime.
405	func (s *aggregateState) containingWindowCount(eventTime int64) int64 {
406		first, last := s.containingWindowBounds(eventTime)
407		return last - first + 1
408	}

410	// containingStart returns the start of the containing window reached back by
411	// offset indices from the last one (offset 0 = last window).
412	func (s *aggregateState) containingStart(eventTime, offset int64) int64 {
413		last := eventTime - eventTime%s.slideMillis
414		return last - offset*s.slideMillis
415	}

417	// firstOverflowingStart reports the start of the earliest containing window
418	// whose end (start + windowMillis) leaves the signed 64-bit range, or -1 when
419	// every containing window fits. Containing starts are an ascending arithmetic
420	// sequence with step slideMillis, so overflow (if any) is a suffix; this
421	// computes its first member directly instead of walking the sequence.
422	func (s *aggregateState) firstOverflowingStart(eventTime int64) int64 {
423		n := s.containingWindowCount(eventTime)
424		lowest := s.containingStart(eventTime, n-1) // earliest containing start; never negative
425		maxSafeStart := int64(math.MaxInt64 - s.windowMillis)
426		if lowest > maxSafeStart {
427			return lowest
428		}
429		safe := (maxSafeStart-lowest)/s.slideMillis + 1 // number of containing starts that fit
430		if safe < n {
431			// Reach back from last, which is at most eventTime, so the
432			// subtraction cannot leave the signed 64-bit range.
433			return s.containingStart(eventTime, n-1-safe)
434		}
435		return -1
436	}

438	func (s *aggregateState) processEvent(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
439		key, err := requiredString(obj, "key", lineNo)
440		if err != nil {
441			return err
442		}
443		if key == "" {
444			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: `field "key" must be a non-empty string`}
445		}
446		eventTime, err := requiredNonNegInt64(obj, "time", lineNo)
447		if err != nil {
448			return err
449		}
450		value, err := requiredInt64(obj, "value", lineNo)
451		if err != nil {
452			return err
453		}
454		p, err := s.requiredPartition(obj, lineNo)
455		if err != nil {
456			return err
457		}
458		if s.partitions > 0 && s.idle[p] {
459			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("event for idle partition %d is not allowed; send a watermark to resume it first", p)}
460		}
461	
462		if s.watermark != nil && eventTime < *s.watermark {
463			notice := fmt.Sprintf("line %d: late event time=%d below current watermark %d, skipped\n", lineNo, eventTime, *s.watermark)
464			if err := writeFull(s.lateLog, []byte(notice)); err != nil {
465				return &OutputError{
466					Line:   lineNo,
467					Kind:   "late-event notice",
468					Detail: fmt.Sprintf("event time %d below current watermark %d", eventTime, *s.watermark),
469					Err:    err,
470				}
471			}
472			return nil
473		}
474	
475		n := s.containingWindowCount(eventTime)
476	
477		// A window whose end leaves the signed 64-bit range is fatal for the
478		// whole input line; check before updating any window state.
479		if badStart := s.firstOverflowingStart(eventTime); badStart >= 0 {
480			return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("window end overflow for key %q window starting at %d with length %d", key, badStart, s.windowMillis)}
481		}
482	
483		// Add the event once to each containing window, in ascending start
484		// order. An overflow here stops processing immediately; already closed
485		// (and thus already written) windows are unaffected.
486		for i := n - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
487			start := s.containingStart(eventTime, i)
488			end := start + s.windowMillis
489			id := windowID{start: start, key: key}
490			st := s.windows[id]
491			if st == nil {
492				st = &windowState{end: end}
493				s.windows[id] = st
494			}
495			if st.count == math.MaxInt64 {
496				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("event count overflow for key %q window [%d,%d)", key, start, end)}
497			}
498			if value > 0 && st.sum > math.MaxInt64-value {
499				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("cumulative sum overflow for key %q window [%d,%d): %d + %d", key, start, end, st.sum, value)}
500			}
501			if value < 0 && st.sum < math.MinInt64-value {
502				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("cumulative sum overflow for key %q window [%d,%d): %d + %d", key, start, end, st.sum, value)}
503			}
504			st.count++
505			st.sum += value
506		}
507		return nil
508	}

510	func (s *aggregateState) processWatermark(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
511		next, err := requiredNonNegInt64(obj, "time", lineNo)
512		if err != nil {
513			return err
514		}
515		p, err := s.requiredPartition(obj, lineNo)
516		if err != nil {
517			return err
518		}
519	
520		if s.partitions == 0 {
521			if s.watermark != nil && next < *s.watermark {
522				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("watermark moved backwards from %d to %d", *s.watermark, next)}
523			}
524			s.watermark = &next
525		} else {
526			resuming := s.idle[p]
527			if resuming {
528				// A resume watermark must be at least the partition's previous
529				// watermark and the effective watermark produced while it was
530				// idle; equality on either boundary resumes.
531				if prev, ok := s.partWatermark[p]; ok && next < *prev {
532					return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("resume watermark %d for partition %d is below its previous watermark %d", next, p, *prev)}
533				}
534				if s.watermark != nil && next < *s.watermark {
535					return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("resume watermark %d for partition %d is below the current effective watermark %d", next, p, *s.watermark)}
536				}
537				delete(s.idle, p)
538			} else if prev, ok := s.partWatermark[p]; ok && next < *prev {
539				return &InputError{Line: lineNo, Reason: fmt.Sprintf("watermark for partition %d moved backwards from %d to %d", p, *prev, next)}
540			}
541			s.partWatermark[p] = &next
542			if effective := s.effectiveWatermark(); effective != nil {
543				s.watermark = effective
544			}
545		}
546	
547		if s.watermark == nil {
548			return nil
549		}
550		return s.closeWindows(*s.watermark, lineNo)
551	}

553	// processIdle declares a partition idle: it stops contributing to the
554	// effective watermark until its next watermark record. The declaration
555	// itself may advance the effective watermark and close windows.
556	func (s *aggregateState) processIdle(obj map[string]json.RawMessage, lineNo int) error {
557		p, err := s.requiredPartition(obj, lineNo)
558		if err != nil {
559			return err
560		}
561		wasIdle := s.idle[p]
562		s.idle[p] = true
563
